introduction: On this Sunday, God says through Isaiah, Behold, I will do a new thing, and promises to blot out our sins. In the Gospel, four friends lower a paralyzed man through a roof to Jesus, who first forgives his sins and then heals him so that he walks. Paul tells us that in Christ every promise of God is Yes. Let us bring one another to Jesus with faith.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord forgives our sins and heals our weakness. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may proclaim with joy that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins. Let us pray to the Lord.
For friends and families who carry the weak and the sick to God in prayer: that their faith may be rewarded. Let us pray to the Lord.
For people living with paralysis or disability: that they may know their dignity and receive care and support. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those weighed down by guilt: that they may hear Jesus say, Your sins are forgiven. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may be faithful friends who bring others to Jesus. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you blot out our sins and remember them no more. Give us the faith of the four friends, so that we may bring others to your Son for healing and forgiveness. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Seeing their faith
reflection.body:
Through Isaiah, God tells his people not to stay stuck in the past: "Behold, I will do a new thing. It springs out now. Don't you know it?" And the new thing he promises is forgiveness: "I, even I, am he who blots out your transgressions for my own sake; and I will not remember your sins."

In the Gospel, Jesus is at home in Capernaum, and the house is so crowded that "there was no more room, not even around the door." Four people bring a paralyzed man on a mat. They cannot get in. So they climb onto the roof, open it up, and lower their friend down in front of Jesus.

Mark tells us that Jesus is struck by what he sees: "Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic": "Son, your sins are forgiven you." It is the faith of the friends that Jesus notices. The man is healed because others carried him.

Some scribes are scandalized: "Who can forgive sins but God alone?" They are right that only God forgives sins, and that is exactly the point. To show that he has this authority, Jesus says to the man, "arise, take up your mat, and go to your house." The man walks out in front of everyone, and they all say, "We never saw anything like this!"

Jesus heals the man's deepest paralysis first: the weight of sin. The Church continues this ministry of forgiveness in the Sacrament of Reconciliation.

Paul tells us that God is faithful: "For however many are the promises of God", in Christ the answer is always Yes.

This week, think of someone you can carry to Jesus through your prayer, your help or your invitation. And if you are carrying the weight of sin, let Jesus say to you, Your sins are forgiven.
